title: Web Accessibility Small Examples
description: Use these small Web Accessibility examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Use a real button
examples.description: A button already knows how to work with a keyboard.
examples.output: The control works with a click, Enter or Space when focused.

examples.title: Give the page a clear outline
examples.description: Headings tell readers how a page is organised.
examples.code:
Our school garden

Plants

We grow beans.

Jobs

Watering

Water in the morning.
examples.output: The page has one main title, two main sections and a smaller watering section.

examples.title: Name important page regions
examples.description: Elements such as nav and main name big page regions.
examples.code:
Garden club

Plants

Plants

Beans grow here.
examples.output: The navigation link moves to the plants content. The main element identifies the main region.

examples.title: Write useful image words
examples.description: Alternative text describes a useful image for someone who cannot see it.
examples.output: A screen reader can describe the seedling and skip the decorative corner flower.

examples.title: Label a form field
examples.description: A visible label explains what to type. Matching its for value with an input id links the two parts.
examples.output: Clicking the label focuses the field. A reading tool can announce Favourite book as its name.

examples.title: Connect help text
examples.description: A field can have a short help message as well as a label.
examples.code: Use the name shown on your club card.
examples.output: A reading tool can announce the field label and then its help text.

examples.title: Keep keyboard focus clear
examples.description: Focus is the place that will receive the next key action.
examples.output: Using Tab moves a visible focus outline between the buttons.

examples.title: Add a skip link
examples.description: A skip link lets a keyboard user move past repeated navigation and straight to the main content.
examples.code:
Skip to main content
Home

Today's reading

Pick a short story.
examples.output: The first link takes the reader to the main region. tabindex=-1 lets that region receive focus without joining the normal Tab order.

examples.title: Make links explain their destination
examples.description: Link words should make sense when read on their own.
examples.code:
Read the garden club timetable

Garden club timetable

We meet on Friday.
examples.output: The link says what it opens and moves to the matching timetable section.

examples.title: Explain a result in words
examples.description: A polite live region can announce a small update without moving keyboard focus.
examples.output: The click adds a status message. A screen reader can announce it when it is ready.

examples.title: Respect less-motion settings
examples.description: Some people feel unwell when a page moves a lot.
examples.code: Reading card
examples.output: The hover lift is removed when reduced motion is requested by the system.

examples.title: Check a page in several ways
examples.description: Accessibility testing needs more than one check.
examples.code:
1. Use Tab and Shift+Tab through the page.
2. Activate controls with Enter or Space.
3. Zoom text and page to 200%.
4. Check labels and error messages.
5. Run an automated accessibility check.
6. Try the main task with a screen reader.
examples.output: You get a list of real problems to fix, such as a hidden focus mark or a field with no label.
